item.title: AI ‘slop’ is a social judgement
item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02639-6

Artificial intelligence (AI)-generated content increasingly saturates our information environment. Efforts to detect and remove it are failing. We propose that calling AI-generated content ‘slop’ is best understood as a social judgement: what a community recognizes as unwanted AI content. Studying AI slop this way makes it tractable, measurable and governable.

item.title: Long-term development of a motor memory
item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02622-1

Franklin et al. examine how simple motor adaptation is developed with thousands of training trials over multiple weeks to study the long-term development of a motor memory.

item.title: A natural field experiment on the effectiveness of economic sanctions before and after the Russian invasion of Ukraine
item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02591-5

A field experiment by Findley et al. finds that financial sanctions on Russian officials had little effect on access to banking and corporate services before the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, but significantly reduced access afterwards.
item.dc:title: A natural field experiment on the effectiveness of economic sanctions before and after the Russian invasion of Ukraine
